After a successful heist, Patricia receives a mysterious anonymous message, informing her, that she has been poisoned by a slow-acting neurotoxin that will leave her completely paralyzed forever in a couple of weeks unless countered by antidote, which will be provided only if she unmasks Mysterik, even though Patricia herself doesn’t know anything about his name or identity. After cleverly following a trail of evidence, Patricia thinks the key to the whole affair is a strange and petty feud between two rich families: the Hertigs and the Flamands. To get to the truth, Patricia has not only to infiltrate both families, befriending Pascal’s wife Alice, and Hertig sisters Caroline and Mireille, but participate in the familial rivalry, which often turns surprisingly destructive and deadly, all while her body gets weaker with every day. Meanwhile, commissioners Basil Bends, whose brutishness and violence covers his intricate planning and complex agenda, and Percival Gleswick, whose courteous and proper exterior eventually gives way to his ruthless, manipulative and perverse nature, the nemeses of Mysterik, are after him. Complicating the matters, Patricia’s ex-fiance Marcel Messier, a sarcastic and offbeat journalist with a deadbeat streak, proceeds with investigations of his own, which threaten to reveal Patricia’s criminal activity. The movie’s editing is dynamic and fast-paced, featuring experimental shots. The more remarkable and unusual scenes are the musical number performed by Mireille Hertig, Patricia’s psychedelic and bizarre nightmares, the hectic car chase and illegal racing sequences, the scene portraying psychological torture invoked on injured Alice by Bends and Gleswick and the rooftop chase sequence.
